title: Do you like spicy food? 🌶️🥵 Improve your listening with Real Easy English

sentences.en: Hello, I'm Neil.
sentences.ko: 안녕하세요, 저는 닐이에요.

sentences.en: And I'm Georgie.
sentences.ko: 그리고 저는 조지예요.

sentences.en: Welcome to Real Easy English.
sentences.ko: Real Easy English에 오신 걸 환영해요.

sentences.en: You can find a worksheet and transcript for this episode on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.ko: 이 에피소드의 학습지와 대본은 웹사이트 bbclearningenglish.com에서 볼 수 있어요.

sentences.en: Hi Georgie. How are you?
sentences.ko: 안녕, 조지. 잘 지내요?

sentences.en: I'm very well, thank you, Neil.
sentences.ko: 아주 잘 지내요, 고마워요, 닐.

sentences.en: Something that made me very happy yesterday was that my housemate made me a delicious meal.
sentences.ko: 어제 정말 기뻤던 게, 하우스메이트가 맛있는 요리를 해 줬어요.

sentences.en: It was very spicy.
sentences.ko: 아주 매웠어요.

sentences.en: Well, we're talking about spicy food today.
sentences.ko: 마침 오늘은 매운 음식에 대해 얘기해요.

sentences.en: Yes. Spicy food is food that makes your mouth hot, and sometimes it can be painful.
sentences.ko: 네. 매운 음식은 입이 화끈거리게 하는 음식이고, 가끔은 아플 수도 있어요.

sentences.en: Neil, I like spicy food.
sentences.ko: 닐, 저는 매운 음식 좋아해요.

sentences.en: What about you?
sentences.ko: 당신은요?

sentences.en: Yeah, I really like spicy food.
sentences.ko: 네, 저도 매운 음식 정말 좋아해요.

sentences.en: I think...
sentences.ko: 제 생각엔...

sentences.en: Well, it has a lot of flavour.
sentences.ko: 음, 맛이 풍부하잖아요.

sentences.en: And it can make you actually feel good when you eat spicy food.
sentences.ko: 그리고 매운 음식을 먹으면 실제로 기분이 좋아질 수 있어요.

sentences.en: It can, kind of, lift your mood.
sentences.ko: 기분을 좀 끌어올려 주죠.

sentences.en: Yeah, I agree actually.
sentences.ko: 네, 사실 저도 동의해요.

sentences.en: Spicy food really makes you feel alive.
sentences.ko: 매운 음식은 정말 살아 있는 느낌을 줘요.

sentences.en: The food that my housemate made for me yesterday was jerk chicken, which she put on the barbecue and it really had a kick.
sentences.ko: 어제 하우스메이트가 해 준 건 저크 치킨이었는데, 바비큐에 구웠고 정말 화끈했어요(had a kick).

sentences.en: So, if something has a kick, it means that it's a little bit spicy.
sentences.ko: 뭔가 'has a kick'이라고 하면 조금 맵다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: So, we had some mayonnaise with it to, kind of, cool it down.
sentences.ko: 그래서 좀 식히려고 마요네즈를 같이 먹었어요.

sentences.en: Yeah, good idea.
sentences.ko: 네, 좋은 생각이네요.

sentences.en: Sometimes when you eat really spicy food or hot food.
sentences.ko: 정말 맵거나 'hot'한 음식을 먹을 때가 있죠.

sentences.en: We say hot food and it doesn't mean the temperature always – it means spicy.
sentences.ko: 'hot food'라고 할 때 늘 온도를 말하는 건 아니에요. 맵다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: When you have spicy food or hot food, it can make it feel like your mouth is on fire.
sentences.ko: 맵거나 'hot'한 음식을 먹으면 입에 불이 난 것 같은 느낌이 들 수 있어요.

sentences.en: Very true.
sentences.ko: 정말 맞아요.

sentences.en: Have you always liked spicy food or was it something you had to learn to love?
sentences.ko: 원래부터 매운 음식을 좋아했어요, 아니면 좋아하게 되기까지 시간이 걸렸어요?

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.ko: 그런 것 같아요.

sentences.en: I think I've always liked spicy food.
sentences.ko: 원래부터 매운 음식을 좋아했던 것 같아요.

sentences.en: Yeah, I've always eaten lots of Indian curries, or Mexican food, or Caribbean food, like your jerk chicken.
sentences.ko: 네, 저는 인도 커리나 멕시코 음식, 아니면 당신의 저크 치킨 같은 카리브 음식을 늘 많이 먹었어요.

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember going on holiday with my family in Spain, and they have a dish there made of peppers, and some of them are very mild so they aren't very spicy, but some of them really have a kick, and
sentences.ko: 네, 가족이랑 스페인에 휴가 갔던 게 기억나요. 거기에 고추로 만든 요리가 있는데, 어떤 건 아주 순해서 별로 안 맵지만 어떤 건 정말 화끈하고,

sentences.en: you don't know which one is going to be really spicy, so it was quite...
sentences.ko: 어떤 게 정말 매울지 모르니까 꽤...

sentences.en: it was almost like an exciting game.
sentences.ko: 거의 신나는 게임 같았어요.

sentences.en: So, I've always enjoyed spice.
sentences.ko: 그래서 저는 늘 매운맛을 즐겼어요.

sentences.en: OK. So, Georgie, you can eat spicier food now than when you were younger.
sentences.ko: 그렇군요. 그러니까 조지, 어렸을 때보다 지금 더 매운 걸 먹을 수 있는 거네요.

sentences.en: Yes. Now, Neil, what's the spiciest meal you've ever eaten?
sentences.ko: 네. 그럼 닐, 지금까지 먹어 본 것 중에 제일 매운 음식은 뭐예요?

sentences.en: Well, I was travelling in South East Asia, and there was something on a menu, in a restaurant or bar I was in, called the spicy sausage salad...
sentences.ko: 음, 동남아시아를 여행할 때였는데, 제가 간 식당인지 바인지 메뉴에 '매운 소시지 샐러드'라는 게 있었어요...

sentences.en: and they weren't lying!
sentences.ko: 그리고 거짓말이 아니었어요!

sentences.en: It was so spicy, it felt almost like somebody had attacked my tongue.
sentences.ko: 너무 매워서 누가 제 혀를 공격한 것 같았어요.

sentences.en: Oh no! Was your mouth on fire?
sentences.ko: 저런! 입에 불이 났어요?

sentences.en: My mouth... My whole head was on fire!
sentences.ko: 입이... 머리 전체에 불이 났어요!

sentences.en: And it took a long time and lots of water before...
sentences.ko: 그리고 한참이 걸렸고 물도 엄청 마셨어요...

sentences.en: before I felt normal again.
sentences.ko: 다시 정상으로 돌아오기까지요.

sentences.en: Does water help?
sentences.ko: 물이 도움이 돼요?

sentences.en: I don't know. I needed to try something.
sentences.ko: 모르겠어요. 뭐라도 해 봐야 했어요.

sentences.en: I think sometimes milk can help, but I don't know if there are...
sentences.ko: 가끔 우유가 도움이 되는 것 같은데, 다른 게 있는지는...

sentences.en: if there's anything else that can help.
sentences.ko: 도움이 되는 다른 게 있는지는 모르겠어요.

sentences.en: But sometimes you really need something to cool down.
sentences.ko: 그래도 가끔은 정말 뭔가로 식혀야 하죠.

sentences.en: Yeah. How about you, Georgie?
sentences.ko: 네. 조지, 당신은요?

sentences.en: What's the hottest thing that you've ever eaten?
sentences.ko: 지금까지 먹어 본 것 중에 제일 매운 건 뭐예요?

sentences.en: Well, it wasn't a meal, but I used to work in a restaurant.
sentences.ko: 음, 식사는 아니었는데, 제가 예전에 식당에서 일했거든요.

sentences.en: And there was a chef there who had three bottles of hot sauce with different levels of spice, and we were all trying it – everyone that worked there – and the spiciest one was so hot.
sentences.ko: 거기 셰프가 매운 정도가 다른 핫소스 세 병을 갖고 있었는데, 거기서 일하는 사람들이 다 같이 먹어 봤어요. 제일 매운 건 정말 너무 매웠어요.

sentences.en: It was so spicy, it...
sentences.ko: 너무 매워서...

sentences.en: my mouth was completely on fire.
sentences.ko: 입에 완전히 불이 났어요.

sentences.en: It was horrible.
sentences.ko: 끔찍했어요.

sentences.en: I actually didn't enjoy that.
sentences.ko: 사실 그건 즐겁지 않았어요.

sentences.en: Everyone was sweating, crying.
sentences.ko: 다들 땀 흘리고, 울고.

sentences.en: I don't think anyone enjoyed the experience.
sentences.ko: 그 경험을 즐긴 사람은 아무도 없었던 것 같아요.

sentences.en: Time now to recap the vocabulary we've heard in this episode, starting with 'spicy'.
sentences.ko: 이제 이번 에피소드에서 들은 어휘를 정리할 시간이에요. 'spicy'부터 시작해요.

sentences.en: If something is 'spicy', it makes your mouth feel hot and that can be uncomfortable or even painful.
sentences.ko: 뭔가가 'spicy'하면 입이 화끈거리고, 불편하거나 심지어 아플 수도 있어요.

sentences.en: We can also describe food as 'hot'.
sentences.ko: 음식을 'hot'이라고 표현할 수도 있어요.

sentences.en: Now, 'hot' is not always about the temperature – it can also mean 'spicy'.
sentences.ko: 'hot'은 늘 온도를 말하는 게 아니에요. 'spicy'라는 뜻일 수도 있어요.

sentences.en: If food is spicy, we can say it 'has a kick'.
sentences.ko: 음식이 매우면 'has a kick'이라고 할 수 있어요.

sentences.en: Now, Georgie said she had some Jamaican jerk chicken and that had a kick – it was spicy.
sentences.ko: 조지가 자메이카식 저크 치킨을 먹었는데 그게 'had a kick', 즉 매웠다고 했죠.

sentences.en: If you eat something that's really spicy, you could say, My mouth is on fire!
sentences.ko: 정말 매운 걸 먹으면 'My mouth is on fire!'라고 할 수 있어요.

sentences.en: And it means it made your mouth feel very hot.
sentences.ko: 입이 아주 화끈거렸다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: If your mouth is on fire, you might want to cool it down with maybe a glass of water or a glass of milk.
sentences.ko: 입에 불이 나면 물 한 잔이나 우유 한 잔으로 식히고(cool it down) 싶을 거예요.

sentences.en: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English, but don't forget to go to our website where you can find a free worksheet and you can test yourself on what you've learned.
sentences.ko: Real Easy English 이번 에피소드는 여기까지예요. 웹사이트에 가면 무료 학습지로 배운 걸 확인할 수 있다는 것도 잊지 마세요.

sentences.en: That's at bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.ko: bbclearningenglish.com이에요.

sentences.en: And we'll be back next week with another conversation in easy English.
sentences.ko: 그리고 다음 주에 쉬운 영어로 된 다른 대화로 돌아올게요.

sentences.en: Goodbye for now.
sentences.ko: 오늘은 여기까지, 안녕히.

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.ko: 안녕!
